messages:
maria_support: Heads-up — customer reported a sudden billing spike (~3x tokens) and a burst of 502/500 around 2025-12-18 15:02 UTC. They say they use the redwood Python sync wrapper inside FastAPI background tasks. Attached logs show repeated retries and an 'Event loop running' error.

alex_sdk: Got it. Do we have the SDK version and a minimal snippet from the customer?

maria_support: They sent this: 
```
# requirements.txt
redwood==0.9.1
fastapi==0.95.0
httpx==0.24.0

# app.py
from fastapi import FastAPI, BackgroundTasks
from redwood import Redwood  # sync wrapper

app = FastAPI()
client = Redwood()

@app.post('/submit')
async def submit(payload: dict, background_tasks: BackgroundTasks):
    # they call the sync client from a background task
    background_tasks.add_task(client.generate, payload)
    return {"ok": True}
```

maria_support: Logs snippet (sanitized):
```
2025-12-18T15:02:03Z ERROR app request_id=... Exception in background task
RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop
  File \"/usr/local/lib/python3.11/asyncio/runners.py\", line 64, in run
  File \"/app/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/sync.py\", line 42, in _run_sync
    return asyncio.run(self._generate_async(...))
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
httpx._exceptions.ConnectError: Connection aborted.
Retrying request (attempt 2/3)
... repeated attempts ...
```

alex_sdk: This screams of the old sync-wrapper pattern in 0.9.x calling asyncio.run() internally. When called from an already running loop (uvicorn/fastapi), it raises and our local retry logic kicks in, causing duplicate outbound calls and extra billable tokens. Also 0.9.1 did not auto-set idempotency for generate endpoints.

tim_infra: Do we have metrics showing retries spiking for that customer account/time window? Can we correlate to increased token usage?

patrick_eng: I pulled logs — from 15:01:58 to 15:03:10 we see ~18 failed attempts followed by 18 successful retries for the same session-id. Token counters show ~3x consumption vs baseline for that integration.

alex_sdk: Root cause is twofold: (1) using the sync wrapper inside an existing event loop causes runtime failure, (2) SDK retries + no idempotency led to duplicate publish of requests. Fix shipped in redwood-py 1.2: the sync wrapper no longer uses asyncio.run() (uses to_thread for sync-to-async) and default idempotency keys are generated for non-idempotent generate calls.

maria_support: Customer is on 0.9.1. They want next steps and whether we can refund.

patrick_eng: Short-term mitigation: ask customer to pin requests to async client or run sync client in a true sync worker. Immediate workaround: set REDWOOD_CLIENT_DISABLE_RETRIES=1 in their env to prevent SDK retries until they can upgrade. Also recommend upgrading to >=1.2.0.

alex_sdk: Sample migration snippet to recommend to customer (async):
```python
from redwood.async_client import RedwoodAsyncClient
client = RedwoodAsyncClient.from_env()

@app.post('/submit')
async def submit(payload: dict):
    # await the async call (or create a background task with asyncio.create_task)
    await client.generate(payload)
```
Or if they need background tasks:
```python
async def worker(payload):
    await client.generate(payload)

@app.post('/submit')
async def submit(payload: dict):
    asyncio.create_task(worker(payload))
    return {"ok": True}
```

tim_infra: I've flagged the account and added a short-term telemetry rule to suppress spikes hitting billing auto-escalation. SRE, can we review for a refund? @sre-bot please create an incident if we need manual billing action.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-20251218-224 — Billing spike investigation (assigned to finance + support).

alex_sdk: Also: ask the customer for the exact account-id and timeframe, and whether they can test upgrading to redwood>=1.2 in a staging env. If they cannot upgrade immediately, advise setting REDWOOD_CLIENT_DISABLE_RETRIES=1 and adding an idempotency_key per request: client.generate(payload, idempotency_key=...)

maria_support: I'll reach out to the customer with these steps and request account-id + trace ids. Will update thread when they respond. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
